classification.difficultyReason: Translate stepped and notched solids into isometric directions while preserving parallel edges and face relationships, then choose two valid triangular-prism drawings using matching translated ends.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw the three solids shown below using isometric paper.

spec.sourceRegion: Original question2a supplied as required given for independent question3a
spec.description: Broad low base with a taller central block, low shoulders, a labelled front stepped face and labelled right side. Decorative blue outlines become black.
spec.mathematics: Uniform-depth stepped prism; two equal-height shoulders flank the raised central section. No numerical dimensions are given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied solid and viewing labels are visible.

spec.sourceRegion: Original question2c supplied as required given for independent question3a
spec.description: Three-level stair solid with two narrow lower treads and a broad top platform; front is the low near end and side is the stepped-profile side.
spec.mathematics: Three equal vertical rises; two short treads precede a longer top platform. Constant transverse width.

spec.sourceRegion: Original question2d supplied as required given for independent question3a
spec.description: Three raised transverse ridges separated by two rectangular channels; long notched side and rectangular front end are labelled.
spec.mathematics: Five longitudinal strips alternate ridge, channel, ridge, channel, ridge; channels have equal depth above a continuous base.

answer.short: Isometric drawings of the three solids, as shown.
answer.worked: Use the vertical and two sloping directions of the isometric paper. Reproduce each solid's outline, then add its visible top and side edges. Keep corresponding edges parallel and preserve the steps and notches.

spec.mathematics: Explicit closed polyhedron with original step/ridge structure; projection basis is vertical and two30degree directions. Hidden edges derived by source-bound face occlusion, not by arbitrary vertex naming.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw two different drawings of a triangular prism on isometric paper.

answer.short: Sample drawings shown. Each has two matching parallel triangular ends joined by three rectangular faces.
answer.worked: Draw a triangle using points on the isometric paper. Draw an identical triangle translated along a third direction, then join corresponding vertices. Repeat with a different triangular cross-section or a different orientation. Show visible edges with solid lines and hidden edges with dashed lines.
